properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by Anthony asking how CI and regression testing here could be improved, 2026-09-21.

THE OBSERVATION, and it is already a recorded incident rather than a worry. On 2026-08-24 every clippy gate passed locally and BOTH CI jobs failed on the same lint with IDENTICAL FLAGS — the compiler version was the narrow gate, and the gate-list cross-check structurally cannot see that axis because it compares command strings, not toolchains. Today `ci.yml` pins ubuntu-22.04 deliberately (to match the release workflow) and takes `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, which is a MOVING TARGET: the same commit builds against a different compiler next month, and nothing in the repo records which one green was measured against.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) PIN THE TOOLCHAIN in `rust-toolchain.toml` so the build is reproducible and a compiler upgrade is a deliberate, reviewable commit rather than a Tuesday. Nearly free, and it converts a class of surprise red into a class of scheduled red. The cost is that nobody upgrades until something forces it.
(b) PIN, PLUS A SCHEDULED JOB ON `stable` — the pinned toolchain gates the build; a nightly or weekly run on floating stable reports drift without blocking anyone. This is the shape reflow2 uses everywhere else: report, do not stop, leave the disposition to a person.
(c) A MATRIX across OS or toolchain. This is where the over-engineering line is: the server ships as a container image and a Linux binary, and there is no recorded case of an OS-specific defect. A matrix multiplies a 60-minute job by the number of cells to guard a class nobody here has been bitten by.
(d) NOTHING — the incident cost one red build and was diagnosed in minutes, which is a real argument that the current arrangement is correctly cheap.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: (c) is almost certainly not worth it; the honest scope of this idea is (a), possibly (b). Worth noting that a pinned toolchain also makes the local gate runner and CI agree on the one axis they currently cannot, which is the actual complaint the recorded incident filed.
properties.name: OPEN — is one toolchain on one OS a wide enough gate, when a gate was already measured to be only as wide as the compiler that ran it?
properties.rationale: Recorded open rather than acted on because the cheap option (a) is nearly uncontroversial and the expensive one (c) guards a class with zero recorded instances here — so the value of the idea is in saying where the line is, not in building the matrix.
